curation.notes: Difficulty is a practical study judgment, not a claim about which words the learner personally knows.

notes: Attach these article contexts to existing canonical IDs; do not replace their lexical fields or use the literary chapter importer.

items.meaning: 承担过多任务或承诺的；工作安排过满的
items.definitionEn: Having accepted more responsibilities than can be handled with the available time or resources.
items.usage: 标题指组织把人员过度分配到多个团队；并非单纯表示投入程度很高。
items.exampleEn: An overcommitted analyst may miss important details even when each project looks manageable alone.
items.exampleZh: 即使每个项目单独看来都能应付，任务过多的分析师也可能漏掉重要细节。

items.meaning: 忙于处理突发问题；四处救急
items.definitionEn: To deal repeatedly with urgent problems instead of planned work.
items.usage: 管理语境为比喻义；强调不断救急，未必解决问题根源。
items.exampleEn: We spent the morning fighting fires instead of preparing the customer workshop.
items.exampleZh: 我们整个上午都在处理突发问题，而没有准备客户研讨会。

items.meaning: 安全失守事件；系统或信息被未经授权访问或泄露的事件
items.definitionEn: An incident in which security protections are violated and protected systems or information are accessed or exposed without authorization.
items.usage: breach 指防护被突破的事件；不应把所有潜在弱点都称为已发生的 breach。
items.exampleEn: The security breach forced two product teams to pause their releases.
items.exampleZh: 这起安全事件迫使两个产品团队暂停发布。

items.meaning: 同时参与多个团队的工作安排
items.definitionEn: An arrangement in which a person belongs to and works on several teams at the same time.
items.usage: 本文核心术语；区别于 multitasking，同一人可以跨团队分时工作。
items.exampleEn: Multiteaming gave the specialist broader experience but fragmented her calendar.
items.exampleZh: 同时参与多个团队让这位专家积累了更广的经验，也使她的日程变得零碎。

items.meaning: 人力资本；人员所具备的知识、技能和能力
items.definitionEn: The knowledge, skills, and abilities that people contribute to productive work.
items.usage: 通常不可数；强调人的能力价值，不把个人简单等同于可替换设备。
items.exampleEn: The firm invested in human capital through mentoring and technical training.
items.exampleZh: 公司通过导师辅导和技术培训投资于人力资本。

items.meaning: 停工或空闲时间；未被有效利用的工作时段
items.definitionEn: A period when a person, machine, or process is not operating or being used.
items.usage: 本文指项目间或项目放缓时的空闲；并非只指系统故障停机。
items.exampleEn: We used the planned downtime to update the team's operating guide.
items.exampleZh: 我们利用计划中的空闲时间更新了团队操作指南。

items.meaning: 在组织内部；由内部人员完成
items.definitionEn: Within an organization rather than through an outside provider.
items.usage: 本文 bring experts in-house 是把专家纳入内部；也可作形容词，如 in-house training。
items.exampleEn: The agency brought the data analysis in-house to improve coordination.
items.exampleZh: 这家机构将数据分析转为内部完成，以改善协调。

items.meaning: 间歇性参与；按需要短暂介入并退出
items.definitionEn: To become involved in an activity for short periods rather than continuously.
items.usage: 常接项目或活动；本文描述专家按需参与，不是完整负责全过程。
items.exampleEn: The architect dips in and out of the project when specialist decisions are needed.
items.exampleZh: 需要作出专业决策时，这位架构师会间歇性参与项目。
collocations: dip in and out of projects
dip in and out of discussions

items.meaning: 传播；广泛分发信息或做法
items.definitionEn: The process of spreading information or ideas to a wider audience.
items.usage: 通常不可数；常用 dissemination of information/knowledge。
items.exampleEn: The internal forum supports the dissemination of lessons from completed projects.
items.exampleZh: 内部论坛帮助广泛传播已完成项目的经验教训。

items.meaning: 可量化的；能够用数字衡量的
items.definitionEn: Able to be measured or expressed as an amount or number.
items.usage: 可量化不等于已被准确测量，也不意味着其他影响不重要。
items.exampleEn: The proposal listed quantifiable savings alongside less tangible learning benefits.
items.exampleZh: 提案同时列出了可量化的节省和较难量化的学习收益。

items.meaning: 群体凝聚力；成员保持团结与联系的程度
items.definitionEn: The strength of the bonds that hold members of a group together.
items.usage: 通常不可数；凝聚力较高不代表成员一定同意所有观点。
items.exampleEn: Frequent staff changes weakened group cohesion during the rollout.
items.exampleZh: 推广过程中频繁的人员变动削弱了群体凝聚力。

items.meaning: 因长期工作压力而出现的精疲力竭与投入下降
items.definitionEn: A state of exhaustion and reduced engagement associated with prolonged work pressure.
items.usage: 工作语境通常不可数；区别于一次短暂疲劳，不把一般忙碌直接诊断为 burnout。
items.exampleEn: The manager reduced overlapping deadlines to lower the risk of burnout.
items.exampleZh: 经理减少了重叠的截止日期，以降低过度耗竭的风险。

items.meaning: 意外出现；突然发生
items.definitionEn: To appear or occur unexpectedly.
items.usage: 不及物；常接问题作主语，不能直接把宾语放在 crop up 后。
items.exampleEn: Several coordination problems cropped up after the teams began sharing a designer.
items.exampleZh: 两个团队开始共用一名设计师后，出现了几个协调问题。

items.meaning: 普遍存在的；广泛流行的
items.definitionEn: Common or widespread in a particular group, place, or period.
items.usage: 常用 prevalent in/among；只说明普遍程度，不评价做法优劣。
items.exampleEn: Shared staffing is prevalent in consulting firms with specialized expertise.
items.exampleZh: 在需要专业技能的咨询公司中，共享人员配置十分普遍。

items.meaning: 同时地；在同一时期并行地
items.definitionEn: At the same time as another activity or event.
items.usage: 本文指项目在时间上重叠，不代表员工在每一秒都同时做两件事。
items.exampleEn: She supported three product launches concurrently during the summer.
items.exampleZh: 夏季期间，她同时为三个产品发布项目提供支持。

items.meaning: 几乎无处不在的；非常普遍的
items.definitionEn: Present or encountered almost everywhere in a relevant setting.
items.usage: 语气强于 common；通常是概括表达，不必理解为绝无例外。
items.exampleEn: Online dashboards are ubiquitous, but teams still need clear ownership of updates.
items.exampleZh: 在线仪表板几乎随处可见，但团队仍需明确谁负责更新。

items.meaning: 通才；知识涉及多个领域而非单一专长的人
items.definitionEn: A person whose knowledge or work covers a broad range of areas.
items.usage: 与 specialist 对照；不等于缺乏专业能力。
items.exampleEn: A generalist coordinated the launch while specialists handled technical decisions.
items.exampleZh: 一名通才协调了发布工作，专业人员则处理技术决策。

items.meaning: 尽量发挥有限资源的作用；使资源承担更多任务
items.definitionEn: To make limited resources cover a wider range or greater amount of work.
items.usage: 也可暗含资源被拉得过紧；需结合上下文判断是否过度。
items.exampleEn: The new contract will stretch resources unless we adjust the delivery plan.
items.exampleZh: 如果不调整交付计划，新合同会让资源更加紧张。

items.meaning: 把某人纳入项目、讨论或信息交流
items.definitionEn: To include someone in an activity or flow of information.
items.usage: 常用 loop someone into a project/discussion；代词放在 loop 与 into 之间。
items.exampleEn: Please loop the support lead into the planning discussion.
items.exampleZh: 请让支持团队负责人加入计划讨论。

items.meaning: 暂时的平静或活动减少；工作空档
items.definitionEn: A temporary period of reduced activity or demand.
items.usage: 通常可数；本文是短暂空档，并非长期闲置。
items.exampleEn: A lull in support requests gave the team time to review recurring issues.
items.exampleZh: 支持请求暂时减少，让团队有时间回顾反复出现的问题。

items.meaning: 任职时长；在某组织工作的年限
items.definitionEn: The length of time a person has worked in a particular role or organization.
items.usage: 本文指服务年限，不是大学里的终身教职制度。
items.exampleEn: As tenure increased, employees often became responsible for more projects.
items.exampleZh: 随着任职年限增加，员工往往需要负责更多项目。

items.originalInput: bringing lessons from one project to bear on others
items.meaning: 把知识、经验或资源运用于某事
items.definitionEn: To apply relevant knowledge, experience, or resources to a problem or situation.
items.usage: 结构为 bring X to bear on Y；bear 在此不表示忍受。
items.exampleEn: She brought her negotiation experience to bear on the supplier dispute.
items.exampleZh: 她运用自己的谈判经验来处理供应商争端。
collocations: bring expertise to bear on a problem
bring experience to bear on a decision

items.meaning: 逐步展开；在实际情境中发展并产生结果
items.definitionEn: To develop or happen over time in a real situation.
items.usage: 本文为不及物发展义；区别于 play out a scene 的演绎义。
items.exampleEn: We waited to see how the new approval process would play out in practice.
items.exampleZh: 我们等待观察新的审批流程在实践中会如何展开。

items.meaning: 可投入的时间、精力或处理能力
items.definitionEn: The time and mental capacity available to handle additional work.
items.usage: 本文是工作能力的比喻义，不是网络带宽；通常不可数。
items.exampleEn: I do not have the bandwidth to review two proposals this afternoon.
items.exampleZh: 我今天下午没有足够的时间和精力审阅两份提案。
collocations: the bandwidth to take on work

items.meaning: 全职当量；折合一名全职员工的工作量单位
items.definitionEn: A unit expressing work capacity as a proportion of one full-time employee's workload.
items.usage: 常缩写 FTE；0.1 FTE 表示约一成全职工作量，不一定对应固定一人。
items.exampleEn: The support task requires half a full-time equivalent over the next quarter.
items.exampleZh: 下一季度，这项支持任务需要相当于半个全职岗位的工作量。

items.meaning: 把任务或人员时间切分成许多小份的做法
items.definitionEn: Dividing something into many small pieces or categories.
items.usage: 本文比喻把人员时间分配给过多项目；也可指把数据按不同维度细分。
items.exampleEn: Endless slicing and dicing of staff time left no space for focused work.
items.exampleZh: 不断细分员工时间，导致没有空间进行专注工作。
collocations: the slicing and dicing of time

items.meaning: 削弱；损害某事的基础或效果
items.definitionEn: To weaken something or make it less effective.
items.usage: 可接信任、信心、权威或收益；不一定指公开反对。
items.exampleEn: Unclear priorities can undermine the benefits of flexible staffing.
items.exampleZh: 不明确的优先事项可能削弱灵活人员配置的好处。

items.meaning: 利用有利条件；充分发挥某事的优势
items.definitionEn: To use an opportunity or advantage to achieve a useful result.
items.usage: 接机会、优势或经验；这里不是把单词首字母大写。
items.exampleEn: The firm capitalized on its regional knowledge when entering the new market.
items.exampleZh: 进入新市场时，公司充分利用了自己的地区知识。

items.meaning: 摩擦；人际或流程之间的阻力与矛盾
items.definitionEn: Tension or difficulty that prevents people or processes from working smoothly together.
items.usage: 本文是比喻义，不是物理摩擦；常用 friction between/among。
items.exampleEn: A clearer handover process reduced friction between the sales and delivery teams.
items.exampleZh: 更清晰的交接流程减少了销售团队和交付团队之间的摩擦。

items.meaning: 防止；抵御不希望发生的问题
items.definitionEn: To prevent something harmful or unwanted from affecting someone.
items.usage: 可分开：ward problems off；宾语为代词时说 ward them off。
items.exampleEn: Agreeing on resource priorities early helped ward off later disputes.
items.exampleZh: 尽早商定资源优先级有助于防止后续争端。

items.meaning: 建立牢固联系；形成紧密关系
items.definitionEn: To create strong relationships between people.
items.usage: forge 在此不是伪造，而是逐步建立；bond 可指人际纽带。
items.exampleEn: Working through the service failure together helped forge bonds across departments.
items.exampleZh: 共同处理服务故障有助于建立跨部门的牢固联系。

items.meaning: 引起猜疑；滋生不信任
items.definitionEn: To create conditions that make people suspicious.
items.usage: breed 的过去式和过去分词为 bred；这里是比喻义。
items.exampleEn: Repeated unexplained delays can breed suspicion among project partners.
items.exampleZh: 反复出现而又没有解释的延误可能使项目伙伴相互猜疑。

items.meaning: 分散在相距很远地点的
items.definitionEn: Spread across places that are far apart.
items.usage: 用于人员、团队或业务网络；作形容词保留连字符。
items.exampleEn: The far-flung team agreed on one shared window for urgent decisions.
items.exampleZh: 这支分布在遥远各地的团队约定了一个共同处理紧急决策的时间段。

items.term: give someone the benefit of the doubt
items.originalInput: give one another the benefit of the doubt
items.meaning: 在证据不足时善意理解某人；姑且相信对方
items.definitionEn: To interpret someone's actions favorably when the available evidence is uncertain.
items.usage: 不是证明对方一定正确；结构为 give someone the benefit of the doubt。
items.exampleEn: I gave the new coordinator the benefit of the doubt and asked why the update was late.
items.exampleZh: 我先善意理解这位新协调员，再询问更新迟交的原因。
forms: gives someone the benefit of the doubt
gave someone the benefit of the doubt
giving someone the benefit of the doubt
collocations: give a colleague the benefit of the doubt
give each other the benefit of the doubt

items.meaning: 对应职位的人；另一组织或地区中职责相当的人
items.definitionEn: A person who has a similar role in another group or organization.
items.usage: 常用 someone's counterpart in/at；不必与本人级别或背景完全相同。
items.exampleEn: Our operations lead contacted her counterpart in the partner company.
items.exampleZh: 我们的运营负责人联系了合作公司中职责对应的人。

items.meaning: 冷淡的；不友好的
items.definitionEn: Showing little warmth or friendliness toward another person.
items.usage: 本文形容人际态度，不是结霜；避免仅凭沉默就断定对方冷淡。
items.exampleEn: His frosty reply made the new team member hesitate to ask another question.
items.exampleZh: 他冷淡的回复让新成员不敢继续提问。

items.meaning: 自视高人一等的；偏向少数精英的
items.definitionEn: Treating a select group as superior or more deserving than others.
items.usage: 本文是对同事态度的初步判断；不等同于某人实际专业能力强。
items.exampleEn: An elitist tone can discourage junior employees from offering useful ideas.
items.exampleZh: 自视高人一等的语气可能让初级员工不愿提出有用的想法。

items.meaning: 信函；书面消息，常带正式或略夸张语气
items.definitionEn: A written message or letter, often formal or lengthy.
items.usage: 较正式，也可略带幽默；本文用于会后发出的书面消息。
items.exampleEn: The lengthy missive explained the concerns that had not come up during the call.
items.exampleZh: 这封长消息解释了通话中没有提到的顾虑。

items.meaning: 敞开心扉谈论；坦诚分享个人想法或情况
items.definitionEn: To speak more freely about personal thoughts, feelings, or experiences.
items.usage: open up about something；本文不是打开物品或开办业务。
items.exampleEn: The kickoff gave people a chance to open up about their development goals.
items.exampleZh: 启动会让大家有机会坦诚分享自己的发展目标。

items.meaning: 坦露不足或不确定性时的脆弱与开放
items.definitionEn: The openness involved in allowing others to see one's limitations, doubts, or need for help.
items.usage: 本文强调信任中的开放，不把暴露技术安全漏洞与此混为一谈。
items.exampleEn: Admitting uncertainty showed vulnerability and made the discussion more honest.
items.exampleZh: 承认不确定性展现了坦诚的脆弱，也使讨论更加真实。

items.meaning: 启动会；项目或团队工作的正式开始
items.definitionEn: An initial event that marks the start of a project or team effort.
items.usage: 名词常写 kickoff；动词写作 kick off，本条只收名词义。
items.exampleEn: The kickoff clarified who would approve changes to the project scope.
items.exampleZh: 启动会明确了由谁批准项目范围的变更。

items.meaning: 同事间相互负责、相互督促的机制
items.definitionEn: Mutual responsibility among colleagues for meeting agreed standards and commitments.
items.usage: peer 指职责关系相近的同事；不是只由上级监督下级。
items.exampleEn: Peer-to-peer accountability helped the team address missed handovers quickly.
items.exampleZh: 同事间相互负责的机制帮助团队迅速处理了交接遗漏。

items.meaning: 事先；在一开始就
items.definitionEn: Before an activity begins or at an early stage.
items.usage: 本文为事先义，不是付款方式；作前置形容词时常写 up-front。
items.exampleEn: We discussed the likely scheduling conflicts up front.
items.exampleZh: 我们事先讨论了可能出现的排期冲突。

items.meaning: 在所有方面或所有相关群体中；全面地
items.definitionEn: In a way that applies to all relevant people, groups, or areas.
items.usage: 常作状语；作前置形容词时写 across-the-board。
items.exampleEn: The change improved response times across the board.
items.exampleZh: 这项变化全面改善了响应时间。

items.meaning: 帮助新成员了解并融入团队或工作流程
items.definitionEn: To help a new employee or member understand a role, process, and team.
items.usage: 及物动词，onboard new members；本条不是介词短语 on board。
items.exampleEn: A short guide helped us onboard two analysts without repeating every explanation.
items.exampleZh: 一份简短指南帮助我们让两名分析师上手，而不用重复每一项说明。

items.meaning: 经验法则；便于实际判断的粗略准则
items.definitionEn: A practical guideline based on experience rather than a precise calculation.
items.usage: 可数；不是适用于所有情况的严格规则。
items.exampleEn: As a rule of thumb, we review team roles after a substantial change in membership.
items.exampleZh: 按照一个经验法则，成员发生较大变化后，我们会重新审视团队角色。

items.meaning: 一组相关的能力、项目或资源组合
items.definitionEn: A collection of activities, skills, or resources considered together.
items.usage: 本文指个人带来的能力组合，不只指投资组合或作品集。
items.exampleEn: The assignment drew on a broad portfolio of technical and client-facing skills.
items.exampleZh: 这项任务需要运用技术能力与面向客户的沟通能力等多方面技能。

items.meaning: 做某事的窍门或特别擅长之处
items.definitionEn: A particular ability to do something skillfully, often with apparent ease.
items.usage: for 后接名词或动名词；常用 have a knack for doing something。
items.exampleEn: He has a knack for turning technical disagreements into clear choices.
items.exampleZh: 他特别善于把技术分歧转化为清晰的选项。

items.meaning: 对某事感到恼火或表现出抵触
items.definitionEn: To react with irritation or defensiveness to something.
items.usage: 常接 criticism、suggestions 或 assignments；at 后接引发抵触的事情。
items.exampleEn: The specialist bristled at the suggestion that she needed no preparation time.
items.exampleZh: 有人暗示这位专家无需准备时间，她对此感到恼火。

items.meaning: 推介；通过介绍方案争取客户或支持
items.definitionEn: To present an idea or service in order to persuade someone to accept or support it.
items.usage: 常用 pitch an idea to someone 或 pitch to a client；本文不是音高或投掷义。
items.exampleEn: The partners pitched a phased rollout to the prospective client.
items.exampleZh: 合伙人向潜在客户推介了分阶段推广方案。
collocations: pitch a proposal to a client

items.meaning: 把某人排除在重要工作之外；使边缘化
items.definitionEn: To prevent someone from taking an active or important role.
items.usage: 本文为动词，不是副业；被动结构 be sidelined 常见。
items.exampleEn: Ignoring her specialist advice sidelined the person best placed to assess the risk.
items.exampleZh: 忽视她的专业意见，使最有条件评估风险的人被边缘化。

items.meaning: 易争吵的；脾气暴躁而难以相处的
items.definitionEn: Bad-tempered and inclined to argue or complain.
items.usage: 比仅表示不同意见语气更强；本文形容受挫后变得难以相处。
items.exampleEn: A cantankerous response made it harder to resolve the staffing dispute.
items.exampleZh: 一个充满火气的回应使人员配置争端更难解决。

items.meaning: 磨炼；不断提高已有技能
items.definitionEn: To improve a skill through focused practice or experience.
items.usage: 常接 skills、expertise 或 judgment；强调精进已有能力。
items.exampleEn: She honed her interviewing skills while working with three different research teams.
items.exampleZh: 她在与三个不同研究团队合作时磨炼了自己的访谈技巧。

items.meaning: 简化并理顺流程，使其更有效率
items.definitionEn: To simplify a process so that it works more efficiently.
items.usage: 及物动词；简化不等于省去所有必要检查。
items.exampleEn: A shared request form streamlined communication between the offices.
items.exampleZh: 一份共用的申请表简化了办公室之间的沟通。

items.meaning: 要求某人对自己的承诺、行为或结果负责
items.definitionEn: To expect someone to explain and take responsibility for performance or results.
items.usage: 结构为 hold someone accountable for something；不只是事后指责。
items.exampleEn: The team agreed to hold each other accountable for timely handovers.
items.exampleZh: 团队同意相互督促，确保按时交接。

items.meaning: 监督；持续检查并指导工作
items.definitionEn: The activity of monitoring work to ensure that it is carried out appropriately.
items.usage: 本文指监督管理，不是 an oversight 所表示的疏漏。
items.exampleEn: The new process reduced routine oversight without removing responsibility for quality.
items.exampleZh: 新流程减少了日常监督，却没有取消质量责任。

items.meaning: 在问题出现前先行地；预先采取措施地
items.definitionEn: In advance, with the aim of preventing an anticipated problem.
items.usage: 强调主动预防；预先行动并不保证所有风险都会消失。
items.exampleEn: We discussed capacity preemptively rather than waiting for another missed deadline.
items.exampleZh: 我们预先讨论了工作容量，而没有等到再次错过截止日期。

items.meaning: 任务或时间压力特别集中的阶段
items.definitionEn: A period when demanding work must be completed under strong time pressure.
items.usage: crunch 在此不是咀嚼声；常指临近截止日期的高压阶段。
items.exampleEn: The two managers moved their reviews to avoid overlapping crunch periods.
items.exampleZh: 两位经理调整了审查时间，以避免高压工作阶段重叠。

items.meaning: 重新调整；大幅改进原有安排
items.definitionEn: To revise or reorganize something substantially in order to improve it.
items.usage: 本文用于重新安排期限；语气通常强于一次小修改。
items.exampleEn: We revamped the meeting schedule after mapping the teams' busiest weeks.
items.exampleZh: 梳理各团队最繁忙的周次后，我们重新调整了会议安排。

items.meaning: 在开始时；起初
items.definitionEn: At the beginning of an activity or process.
items.usage: 常用 at the outset of something；不能换成 in the outset。
items.exampleEn: At the outset, we agreed which decisions required the full team's input.
items.exampleZh: 一开始，我们就商定了哪些决策需要全体团队成员参与。
collocations: at the outset of a project

items.meaning: 关键时点；对后续走向很重要的阶段
items.definitionEn: An important point at which decisions or events can strongly affect what follows.
items.usage: juncture 指特定阶段或时点；critical 在此不是批评性的。
items.exampleEn: A short check-in at a critical juncture prevented the two workstreams from diverging.
items.exampleZh: 关键时点的一次简短沟通，防止了两条工作线走向不同方向。

items.meaning: 暂时帮助某人渡过困难或填补空档
items.definitionEn: To provide enough support for someone until a fuller solution becomes available.
items.usage: 代词放在 tide 与 over 之间，如 tide us over；强调暂时支持。
items.exampleEn: A brief video update can tide us over until the full review next week.
items.exampleZh: 一段简短的视频更新可以在下周完整审查前暂时满足我们的需要。
collocations: tide someone over until a meeting
tide us over for a week

items.meaning: 察觉信号；注意到暗示情绪或状态的线索
items.definitionEn: To notice signs that reveal information about a person's feelings or situation.
items.usage: pick up 在此是察觉，不是捡起；常用 cues about stress 或 cues from body language。
items.exampleEn: Video calls helped the manager pick up cues about the team's workload.
items.exampleZh: 视频通话帮助经理察觉团队工作负荷方面的信号。

items.meaning: 挤占；排挤掉其他活动的空间或时间
items.definitionEn: To displace something because competing demands use up the available space or resources.
items.usage: 常用 be crowded out by；代词宾语放中间，如 crowd it out。
items.exampleEn: Urgent reporting requests crowded out time for learning and reflection.
items.exampleZh: 紧急的报告要求挤占了学习和反思的时间。

items.meaning: 达到预期；不辜负期望
items.definitionEn: To perform as well as people expected.
items.usage: 常用 live up to someone's expectations；这里 live 不表示居住。
items.exampleEn: The pilot did not live up to expectations, so we reviewed the original assumptions.
items.exampleZh: 试点未达到预期，因此我们重新审视了最初的假设。
collocations: fail to live up to expectations

items.meaning: 日复一日；持续不断地
items.definitionEn: Repeatedly over a long period, often as part of a routine.
items.usage: 强调长期反复；也常见 day in, day out。
items.exampleEn: She modeled careful listening day in and day out until it became a team habit.
items.exampleZh: 她日复一日地示范认真倾听，最终使之成为团队习惯。
collocations: work day in and day out
practice day in and day out
do something day in and day out

items.meaning: 报复性惩罚；因某种行为而受到的惩处
items.definitionEn: Punishment imposed in response to behavior regarded as wrong.
items.usage: 本文 fear of retribution 指员工担心报告错误后受到惩罚；通常不可数。
items.exampleEn: People reported small mistakes earlier when they no longer feared retribution.
items.exampleZh: 不再害怕受到惩罚后，大家更早地报告了小错误。

items.meaning: 指定；任命某人承担特定职责
items.definitionEn: To choose someone or something for a particular role or purpose.
items.usage: 常用 designate someone to do something 或 designate someone as a lead。
items.exampleEn: The director designated two members to coordinate the customer handover.
items.exampleZh: 主管指定了两名成员协调客户交接。

items.meaning: 交叉培训；学习彼此岗位或专业的技能
items.definitionEn: To learn or teach skills beyond a person's usual responsibilities.
items.usage: 既可说 employees cross-train，也可说 cross-train employees；本文不是体育训练。
items.exampleEn: We cross-trained two coordinators so that either could handle urgent bookings.
items.exampleZh: 我们对两名协调员进行了交叉培训，让任何一人都能处理紧急预约。

items.meaning: 尽自己应尽的一份责任；承担合理份额的工作
items.definitionEn: To contribute a fair share of the effort required by a group.
items.usage: 强调公平贡献，不只是工作时间很长；one's 随主语改变。
items.exampleEn: Everyone needs a visible responsibility so that we can tell whether each person is pulling their weight.
items.exampleZh: 每个人都需要明确可见的责任，这样才能判断大家是否尽到了应尽的那份义务。
collocations: pull one's weight on a team
expect colleagues to pull their weight

items.meaning: 松懈；少做本应完成的工作
items.definitionEn: To reduce effort or work less than expected.
items.usage: 本文指贡献不足；区别于名词 slack 所指的备用容量。
items.exampleEn: Even after the deadline was extended, the team agreed not to slack off.
items.exampleZh: 即使截止日期被推迟，团队仍约定保持投入，不松懈。

items.meaning: 缓和紧张局势；降低冲突的激烈程度
items.definitionEn: To make a tense or potentially harmful situation less intense or dangerous.
items.usage: 比喻义；区别于 diffuse 的扩散义；缓和不一定等于完全解决。
items.exampleEn: Acknowledging both teams' pressures helped defuse the argument about staffing.
items.exampleZh: 承认两个团队都面临压力，有助于缓和人员配置方面的争执。

items.meaning: 相互依赖；彼此的行动会影响对方的关系
items.definitionEn: A relationship in which people or groups depend on or affect one another.
items.usage: interdependence 常不可数；本文还出现 interdependency，核心意思相近。
items.exampleEn: Mapping interdependence showed why a delay in one team affected three others.
items.exampleZh: 梳理相互依赖关系，揭示了为什么一个团队的延误会影响另外三个团队。

items.meaning: 分散的；没有集中在少数地点或群体中的
items.definitionEn: Spread across a wide area or many groups rather than concentrated in a few places.
items.usage: 本文描述团队共享成员的分布方式，不必特指地理距离。
items.exampleEn: Dispersed overlap meant that the staffing change affected many teams slightly.
items.exampleZh: 成员重叠关系较分散，意味着这次人员变化对许多团队都造成了轻微影响。

items.meaning: 不成比例地；相对于基准显得过大或过小地
items.definitionEn: To a degree that is unusually large or small relative to a relevant comparison.
items.usage: 常与 large、small 或 affected 搭配；需说明相对于什么不成比例。
items.exampleEn: The shared specialist's absence affected the smallest team disproportionately.
items.exampleZh: 共用专家的缺席对最小团队造成了不成比例的影响。

items.meaning: 所有可用人员都来帮忙；全员应急投入
items.definitionEn: A call for everyone available to help with an urgent or demanding task.
items.usage: 来自船上全员到甲板的表达；管理语境通常为紧急动员。
items.exampleEn: The service outage became an all-hands-on-deck situation for the support group.
items.exampleZh: 这次服务中断成了支持团队需要全员投入的紧急情况。
collocations: call for all hands on deck
all hands on deck during a crisis

items.meaning: 对模糊性和不确定性的容忍与适应能力
items.definitionEn: The ability to work despite unclear information, roles, or outcomes.
items.usage: ambiguity 通常不可数；容忍模糊不等于不需要澄清关键责任。
items.exampleEn: Cross-functional projects often require tolerance for ambiguity during their early stages.
items.exampleZh: 跨职能项目在初期往往需要对模糊性有一定容忍能力。

items.meaning: 被当作可互换商品或标准化资源的
items.definitionEn: Treated as interchangeable units with little recognition of distinctive value.
items.usage: 本文指员工感觉个人能力与身份不受重视，不是一般的资源共享。
items.exampleEn: Employees felt commoditized when staffing decisions ignored their interests and expertise.
items.exampleZh: 人员配置决策忽视个人兴趣和专长时，员工觉得自己被当成了可替换资源。

items.meaning: 全局视角；对整体关系的概览
items.definitionEn: A broad view of a situation that shows how its main parts fit together.
items.usage: 比喻义；强调整体结构而非所有细节；也常写 birds-eye 的误拼应避免。
items.exampleEn: The staffing map gave us a bird's-eye view of shared responsibilities.
items.exampleZh: 人员配置图让我们从全局看清了共用人员承担的责任。
collocations: a bird's-eye view of the organization

items.meaning: 易受某事影响或损害的
items.definitionEn: Likely to be affected or harmed by a particular influence or problem.
items.usage: to 后接名词或动名词；通常用于不利影响，而不是所有中性变化。
items.exampleEn: Teams with one irreplaceable specialist are susceptible to sudden disruption.
items.exampleZh: 只有一名不可替代专家的团队容易受到突发中断的影响。

items.meaning: 以身作则；用自己的行为示范要求
items.definitionEn: To guide others by behaving in the way one expects them to behave.
items.usage: 不仅是给出一个口头例子；lead 的过去式、过去分词为 led。
items.exampleEn: The director led by example by sharing lessons from her own failed project.
items.exampleZh: 主管分享了自己失败项目中的经验，以此以身作则。
collocations: lead by example in sharing knowledge

items.meaning: 效仿；采取与别人相似的行动
items.definitionEn: To do something similar to what another person or group has already done.
items.usage: suit 不加冠词；此处不是跟随某套西装或提起诉讼。
items.exampleEn: After one team published its lessons, several others followed suit.
items.exampleZh: 一个团队公布经验教训后，其他几个团队也纷纷效仿。

items.meaning: 午餐学习交流会；常由参与者自带午餐的非正式活动
items.definitionEn: An informal meeting or learning session held during lunch, often with participants bringing food.
items.usage: 管理语境常指午间分享活动；不是泛指所有装在纸袋里的午餐。
items.exampleEn: A monthly brown-bag lunch helped engineers share practical testing lessons.
items.exampleZh: 每月一次的午餐交流会帮助工程师分享实际测试经验。

items.meaning: 特意去做；把某件事当作有意坚持的做法
items.definitionEn: To deliberately ensure that something is done.
items.usage: of 后接动名词，如 make a point of sharing；不是表达一个论点。
items.exampleEn: The manager made a point of thanking people who helped another team.
items.exampleZh: 经理特意感谢了帮助其他团队的员工。
collocations: make a point of sharing lessons
make a point of acknowledging contributions

items.meaning: 亲身体验陈述；说明某种做法价值的见证或评价
items.definitionEn: A statement describing personal experience with or support for something.
items.usage: 本文是员工介绍跨团队学习收益的陈述，不是法庭证词的特定义。
items.exampleEn: The workshop included a testimonial from a coordinator who had used the new process.
items.exampleZh: 研讨会上，一位使用过新流程的协调员分享了亲身体验。

items.meaning: 缓冲；减轻某种冲击造成的影响
items.definitionEn: To reduce the impact of a difficulty or shock.
items.usage: buffer 可作名词或动词；本条为动词结构 buffer against shocks，不承诺彻底防止。
items.exampleEn: A small reserve of specialist time buffered the team against sudden requests.
items.exampleZh: 少量预留的专家时间缓冲了突发请求对团队的冲击。

items.meaning: 备用时间、人员或处理能力；资源余量
items.definitionEn: Spare capacity that allows a system or team to absorb unexpected demands.
items.usage: 本文为不可数名词，不是懒散；区别于动词短语 slack off。
items.exampleEn: We built some slack into the schedule to absorb urgent customer issues.
items.exampleZh: 我们在日程中预留了一些余量，以应对紧急客户问题。

items.meaning: 无所事事地等待；闲着没事做
items.definitionEn: To spend time waiting without doing anything useful.
items.usage: 本文否认保留资源余量就等于无所事事；one's 随主语改变。
items.exampleEn: The spare engineer was not twiddling her thumbs; she was preparing the recovery checklist.
items.exampleZh: 这位暂时空闲的工程师并没有无所事事，而是在准备恢复清单。

items.meaning: 节奏或内容的变化；不同于日常的调剂
items.definitionEn: A different activity or routine that provides variety from usual work.
items.usage: 常用 a welcome change of pace；不只指速度变快或变慢。
items.exampleEn: The customer workshop was a welcome change of pace from routine data cleaning.
items.exampleZh: 与日常数据清理相比，这次客户研讨会是令人愉快的工作调剂。

items.originalInput: exempting members of those teams from answering
items.meaning: 使某人免于某项要求、义务或安排
items.definitionEn: To free someone from a requirement or obligation that would otherwise apply.
items.usage: from 后接名词或动名词；也可用 be exempt from，语气不表示普遍免除责任。
items.exampleEn: We exempted the launch team from routine reporting during the final testing week.
items.exampleZh: 在最后一周测试期间，我们免除了发布团队的常规报告任务。
collocations: exempt a team from routine meetings

items.meaning: 受到打击或损失；遭受不利影响
items.definitionEn: To suffer damage, loss, or a negative effect.
items.usage: 本文是团队项目受冲击的比喻义，不是实际被击打。
items.exampleEn: Service quality took a hit when both experienced coordinators were reassigned.
items.exampleZh: 两名经验丰富的协调员都被调走后，服务质量受到了影响。

items.meaning: 微观管理；对工作细节进行过度控制
items.definitionEn: Excessively close control of how other people carry out their work.
items.usage: 通常不可数；必要监督不自动等于 micromanagement。
items.exampleEn: Asking for hourly explanations made the new tracking system feel like micromanagement.
items.exampleZh: 要求每小时解释工作情况，使新的跟踪系统让人感觉像是过度管理。

items.meaning: 行动或决策的自由；自主空间
items.definitionEn: Freedom to act or make decisions without close control.
items.usage: rein 指缰绳，不是 reign；常用 give someone free rein to do something。
items.exampleEn: The sponsor gave the team free rein to choose its research methods.
items.exampleZh: 项目发起人给予团队自主选择研究方法的空间。

items.meaning: 未受到检查、约束或纠正；任其发展
items.definitionEn: To continue without being examined, limited, or corrected.
items.usage: 常用于风险、问题或行为；unchecked 不是未勾选复选框的意思。
items.exampleEn: Conflicting priorities went unchecked until two important deadlines collided.
items.exampleZh: 相互冲突的优先事项一直未受到协调，直到两个重要截止日期撞在一起。
